 5 Red Dead Redemption 2 Features That Are Officially Returning In GTA 6
 By   Pauli Poisuo 
 Nov. 20, 2026 12:00 pm EST 
 Rockstar Games 
 Add SVG on Google: 
 Preferred Source 
 Google Discover 
 It's "Grand Theft Auto" season, and the new game might be more realistic than anyone expected. Rockstar Games' long-gestating magnum opus has been available for preloading for PS5 and Xbox since November 10 , and fans finally get to find out what it's like to play the eagerly awaited game on November 19. SVG's guide for everything you need to know about "GTA VI" is your friend — but even with all the information about the game already out there, some questions remain.
 One thing that will no doubt interest gamers is just how much of the previous Rockstar titles "GTA VI" intends to incorporate. Considering the game's increased focus on realistic antics, a particularly significant question is just how many mechanics from Rockstar's current king of realism, "Red Dead Redemption 2," will make it into Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval's adventures in one form or another. Here's a look at the "RDR2" features that are on their way to "GTA VI."
 The honor system
 Rockstar Games 
 Outside the predetermined missions, fans have been able to play "Grand Theft Auto" games with the exact amount of morality — or lack thereof – that they feel like for ages. However, "GTA VI" will kick things up a notch and actually make the player's honor a central feature in the game. 
 This, of course, is not a new thing for Rockstar. The honor system is familiar kit from "Red Dead Redemption 2," where Arthur Morgan could be played on a sliding scale of nobility and heroism. The results impact social reactions, cutscenes, in-game perks, and even the game's ending. 
 The feature is set to make its return in "GTA VI" — with a twist, of course. Though they can't outright break up (unless the game chooses to throw that plot twist at us at some point), the game will keep track on Lucia and Jason's relationship based on their actions toward each other and adjust accordingly. This mechanic also has the potential to impact the game's ending. 
 An even closer relative to the familiar "RDR2" honor system is the criminal profile. Your reputation on the street and in the eyes of the law will affect the way the game unfolds, and outside self-defense, every violent situation you escalate will add to your criminal profile. Passersby might recognize you as a person to avoid, and cops will remember your appearance long after you commit atrocities. On the other hand, acting like a decent, law-abiding citizen will have a positive effect on your reputation. We'll see just how deep Rockstar intends to dive down this improved honor system rabbit hole, but considering the game's overall scale, prepare for something truly extensive.
 Interactive safehouses
 Rockstar Games 
 One of the most entertaining and effective features of "Red Dead Dedemption 2" are the camp sites the Van der Linde Gang sets up over the course of the game. From the snowy hellscape of Colter in the beginning of the game to the idyllic camp of Horseshoe Overlook and the ratty despair pit of Beaver Hollow, the various camps act as an important storytelling device that reflects the gang's overall mood and tensions. They offer copious interactive things to do, from partaking in chores and minigames to just wandering around the camp and seeing what the other gang members are up to. 
 With "Grand Theft Auto VI," Rockstar intends to bring a version of this fun feature to the safehouses the player characters reside in. The game's safehouses will be far more interactive than what we've seen so far, considerably expanding on the existing but comparatively austere "click to drink a beer and watch TV"-style mechanics we saw in "GTA V." While it seems unlikely that these safehouses will have Van der Linde Gang levels of people hanging around all the time, the houses themselves will feature plenty of interactive mechanisms, including a "RDR2"-style ability to groom the player character and change their appearance to an extent. 
 Dead Eye targeting
 Rockstar Games 
 A key feature in the "Red Dead" games is the Dead Eye system, which enables the player to target enemies in slow motion, with various frills added in. "Grand Theft Auto V" already introduced a version of this ability with Michael De Santa's Area Kill bullet time special ability, but it looks like "GTA VI" intends to further expand on the concept. 
 The game has what looks an awful lot like a version of the "RDR2" Dead Eye meter. In "GTA VI," the feature is called Focus. It's available to both player characters, and much like Dead Eye, it can be used to pinpoint weaknesses in enemies. Apart from the Focus ability's traditional use in gunplay situations, it will also incorporate a version of the hunting-themed Eagle Eye skill from "RDR2," expanding it to apply to various non-combat situations where Lucia and Jason need to observe and locate threats and points of interest.
 Studying animals
 Rockstar Games 
 For the peaceful "Red Dead Redemption 2" player, one of the more rewarding side activities in the game is the hobby of studying animals for your compendium. The numerous species in the game can be observed, hunted, or fought. There are also various legendary animals that you can track down, which double as optional boss fights.  
 Animals and zoological studies will be back with a vengeance for "Grand Theft Auto VI," as the lush Leonida will feature over 170 species for you to observe and learn about. Given the presence of the Focus mechanic and the fact that hunting already played a limited role in "GTA V," it's also pretty safe to assume that the player will also be able to track and hunt various creatures in "GTA VI." After all, Rockstar has already confirmed that there will be a host of rare and legendary creatures for the player to encounter. 
 Oh, and yes, of course you can pet the dogs in "GTA VI," just like you could in "RDR2." Rockstar knows what the people want. 
 The greeting system
 Rockstar Games 
 Since "Grand Theft Auto VI" incorporates a version of the "Red Dead Redemption 2" honor system, it's only natural for it to tinker with the Western game's greeting system, as well. In "RDR2," the player can choose to verbally either greet or antagonize just about every NPC they meet, and the results can range from heartwarming to hilarious. 
 The "GTA VI" dialogue system works in a similar fashion as the "RDR2" one, though it seems to offer considerably more situational options. When the player approaches a character that can be talked with, a button-based dialogue system at the bottom of the screen will initiate. The system seems intuitive and more interactive than anything Rockstar has offered to date, and since "GTA V" already featured a simple version of talking to random NPCs, there's every chance to believe that the "GTA VI" dialogue system will function as a vastly improved version of both that and the "RDR2" greet/antagonize system.
